turnaround_reason: Sarepta's DMD gene therapy Elevidys was hit by three patient deaths (fatal liver failure), an FDA distribution suspension and clinical holds, a boxed warning, and a label restriction to ambulatory patients only. The stock fell to ~$20; 'recovering' reflects the FDA-cleared ambulatory restart, but this is a genuinely damaged franchise.
bullish_points: FDA cleared a restart of Elevidys shipments for ambulatory patients after clearing an unrelated Brazil death — worst-case distribution shutdown avoided
Balance sheet cushion: cash ~$788M vs debt ~$1.06B, current ratio 4.4; aggressive 36% workforce cut extends runway
Recent EPS beats (Q2 0.64 vs 0.49) and a very cheap fwd P/E ~7.9 if the base PMO/RNA franchise stabilizes
Pivot toward siRNA platform gives a longer-term pipeline story beyond the impaired gene-therapy program
bearish_points: Three deaths and a boxed warning on the flagship product — a safety overhang that can resurface with any new adverse event
Label now restricted to ambulatory DMD only; non-ambulatory and limb-girdle programs are curtailed, structurally shrinking the addressable market
Revenue collapsing (-34% TTM); the deep workforce cut signals management itself is bracing for a much smaller company
Analyst target range is $5 to $38 (mean ~$22) — extreme disagreement means the outcome is binary and headline-driven, not analyzable with confidence
catalyst: Clean safety data through the ambulatory relaunch plus siRNA pipeline progress that reframes the story beyond Elevidys
suggested_trade: Pass for a turnaround book. This is an event-driven biotech gamble on safety headlines, not a fundamentals-driven recovery; if played at all, tiny defined-risk options only.
key_risk: Another Elevidys adverse event or death re-triggers FDA action, gutting the remaining ambulatory franchise and the equity with it.
would_skip_if: Any new serious safety signal emerges, or the ambulatory relaunch shows weak uptake — either would confirm the franchise is permanently impaired.
